sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Three old iPhones and an iPad, synced live in Final Cut Pro: Apple's Live Multicam, found by accident.
sections.para: Gabriel filmed a three-camera video with two second-hand iPhone 12s and an iPhone 13 connected to an iPad. Live Multicam, released on 20 June 2024 with the free Final Cut Camera app, records up to four angles in sync, transfers full-quality files afterwards and moves to the Mac for the edit. He found it by accident, which suggests many who could use it do not know it exists.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Up to four angles, a free camera app, full-quality files after, and the edit on the Mac.
sections.para: Apple released Live Multicam in Final Cut Pro for iPad 2.0. The iPad's own camera can be one of the angles, phones need to be an iPhone XS or later, and the project exports to Final Cut Pro on the Mac.

sections.label: How he found it
sections.line: It came out while he explained the Separate Ways video: he discovered it by accident.
sections.para: He bought old phones on purpose because he only needed the cameras, and connected them to an iPad running Final Cut Pro for what he called a live show.

sections.label: What it is
sections.line: Each phone runs Final Cut Camera; the iPad shows and controls every angle live.
sections.para: Apple announced it on 7 May 2024. The iPad works from synced live previews, each device records its own full-quality file that transfers afterwards with both apps open, and the project exports to the Mac.

sections.label: What it needs
sections.line: An iPhone XS or later, an iPad with M1, A16 or A17 Pro, a free app and a subscription.
sections.para: Final Cut Pro for iPad is sold in the Creator Studio bundle since January 2026. Apple's pages gave different minimum operating system versions on the day checked.

sections.label: What it is good for
sections.line: Music videos, interviews and podcasts, small shows, lessons and teaching.
sections.para: Several synced angles from devices many people already own, without a crew.

sections.label: Why this is its own article
sections.line: A working producer found it by accident, and coverage went quiet after launch.
sections.para: There are no usage figures, so little known rests on one data point. Publishing what you discover at the moment you discover it is the point.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: His setup as described; Apple's requirements as read on the day; little known is an impression.
sections.para: Live Multicam was not tested by the author, and requirements change with each release.
